correctness.rationale: The base automaton tracks the three binary carries for n+d, n+2d and n+3d and the XOR of their digit sums with n; its 2*3*4*8=192 states are exhaustive because each carry c_j remains at most j. Reverse reachability through high zero digits of d accounts for every remaining digit of n and every final carry. The generated determinized 195-state reachability graph is exhaustively traversed, and the exact three terminal masks 0x6e (5 states), 0xf7 (6), and 0xff (184) are checked at every reachable state. Exhaustive transition closure proves their exact occurrence at odd differences 1,3,and >=5. Complement symmetry gives twice the relative-mask population, and binary scaling removes powers of two. The verifier independently constructs witnesses and checks actual digit sums; no infinite conclusion is based solely on a finite prefix.

originality.rationale: The 2021 source addresses maximum monochromatic progression length and mentions only all-difference arithmetical universality. The 2025 source already proves four-term monochromatic existence for all non-powers of two; that known mask-0 implication is explicitly credited. Neither inspected full text covers the complete fixed-difference incidence set or its 14-pattern odd-part-three exception. Actual semantic searches for fixed differences, 0110/1001, and the 10/14/16 spectrum found no covering theorem. The foundational 2003 paper was accessible via bibliographic and secondary statements but not full body, retained as a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed note or automata appendix may have computed the exact fixed-difference 4-pattern table.
The complete body of the 2003 foundational paper was not inspected; its accessible summaries describe a weaker quantifier, but unreported fixed-step tables cannot be categorically excluded.
The result is specific to length four; higher lengths may have substantially more exceptional odd parts.

value.rationale: Determining which words occur along a prescribed arithmetic step refines the natural arithmetical-complexity invariant and the extensively studied fixed-step monochromatic Thue–Morse problem. The result is a complete all-difference structural classification rather than a finite slice: it identifies exactly the unique nontrivial odd part 3 obstruction and gives all 16 patterns for every other odd part >=5. Its proof uses a rigorously closed finite-state quotient and provides reproducible exact certificates.
